title: test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process declares PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300, so its 129 s wall is not read as a 120 s timeout
intention: test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py declares a top-level PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300, and the tester's run_proof runs it at that budget.
why: Measured 2026-11-19: 2026-11-19 on akiendell (Windows), origin/main f56f0f8fd: bin/cairn test at the default 120 s budget TIMED OUT (nothing written); at --timeout 540 it finished in 129 s wall (7 of 8 teeth pass; the one red, test_the_moved_proofs_stay_green, is the librarian's test_librarian_trees.py, queued for a Linux read, not a timeout). Its slow tooth runs the four _MOVED sibling proofs as subprocesses (timeout=300 each). aa750de17382 (PROVED) fixed the fork, not the budget. Law 7: a timeout is a measurement of the budget, not a red of the proof.
traces_to: Law 3 (the budget is measured wall plus margin); Law 4 (the budget is the proof's own byte).
how: A hypothesis, measured by the proof: add `PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300` at the top level of cairn/devices/db_domain/proofs/test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py. Budget = measured wall plus margin: 129 s idle on Windows, so 300 s is 2.3x it and 2.5x the 120 s default that already timed it out. No Linux wall is read yet; if akienasus measures above 300 s the number is re-measured, not guessed up. The mechanism is 8383a32d20c5's; aa750de17382 is PROVED, so this is a new ticket, not a decision on it.
